items.excerpt: A small scene of producers is deliberately making 'anti-bangers' — deformed, unquantised, structurally hostile tracks — as a form of data poisoning against music models that scrape streaming catalogues. CDM frames it as an emerging genre where making music that AI can't learn from becomes the creative constraint.
items.title: Music to confuse AI might be the next new genre

items.excerpt: Federico Pepe built Push Hack, an unauthorised SSH toolkit that opens Ableton Push 3 standalone's display, file system, MIDI and LEDs to custom code — and he built it largely with AI-assisted coding agents. It is a working example of instrument-makers using LLM agents to reverse-engineer and extend closed hardware.
items.keyword: AI in Ableton / AI-assisted instrument hacking
items.title: Push Hack, very unauthorized access to Push 3's display, files, MIDI, and more

items.excerpt: Dreamtonics — the studio behind Synthesizer V Studio and the real-time voice-morphing plug-in Vocoflex — has teased a new product with a single line: 'human nuance is not a switch.' The tease points at the next step in AI vocal synthesis being about expressive control rather than one-click replacement.
items.title: Dreamtonics tease upcoming release: 'human nuance is not a switch'

items.excerpt: Thomas Bangalter says he is 'not really interested in the creative usage of artificial intelligence', arguing that prompt-driven tools force creation through language while his own process happens at a level that 'does not express itself through words'. A pointed craft critique of text-to-music from one of electronic music's most machine-literate artists.
items.title: Daft Punk's Thomas Bangalter: 'I'm not really interested in the creative usage of AI'

items.excerpt: Distributor Symphonic is bundling ArtyShield's MusicShield into its artist toolkit: the tech subtly alters acoustic features of a recording so AI models can't cleanly learn from it, alongside VeriTune AI-detection and VoiceShield anti-voice-cloning. Adversarial protection is moving from research demo to a checkbox in the release workflow.
items.keyword: AI vocal cloning / artist protection tooling
items.title: Symphonic partners with ArtyShield to give artists tools that protect their music and voices from unauthorized AI use

items.excerpt: An op-ed arguing the industry is obsessing over AI detection — guessing the recipe after dinner is served — when what creators need is provenance captured while the work is being made. With TIDAL already using AI labels to gate royalties, 'metadata becomes money' and the credit trail has to start in the session, not the audit.
items.title: The Music Industry Is Trying to Guess the AI Recipe After Dinner Was Served

items.excerpt: Austin Rockman's free, open-source Reflector analyses your own sample library locally with machine learning and lets you browse it by harmonic relationship rather than folder names. It is generative-free AI for producers: the model finds what you already own instead of inventing new audio.
items.keyword: AI sample generation / ML sample discovery
items.title: Reflector is a FREE open-source sample discovery workstation for macOS

items.excerpt: Suno's CEO insists the company is building 'responsibly' and won't leave musicians behind, as it commits to watermarking generated audio and capping downloads to curb mass distribution. The framing matters for anyone building a workflow on Suno: the product is being reshaped by label pressure in real time.
items.title: Suno CEO insists Suno is 'responsible' and isn't going to leave people behind

items.excerpt: Suno will embed inaudible audio watermarks in generated tracks and impose download limits so AI songs can be identified downstream by platforms and rights holders. For creators shipping Suno-assisted material, provenance is now baked into the file itself.
items.title: Suno is adding audio watermarks so AI-generated songs are more easily identifiable

items.excerpt: Musixmatch's Sentinel — real-time fingerprinting that flags copyrighted compositions and recordings at high volume — has signed its first customer: Suno. Generation platforms are starting to run rights-detection at the point of creation rather than after upload.
items.keyword: music AI licensing / detection at generation time
items.title: Musixmatch's first customer for its fingerprinting and detection tech is Suno

items.excerpt: Suno published a formal set of principles around 'artistry and creativity', pairing them with download restrictions and audio fingerprinting aimed at streaming-farm abuse. Music Ally reads the document as a pre-settlement posture as much as a creative manifesto.
items.title: Suno publishes set of principles showing 'support for artistry and creativity'

items.excerpt: 'Human-made' badges are spreading across stores and streaming services, but the piece argues nobody can actually verify them: there is no shared definition of how much AI is too much, and no distributor-level disclosure to check against. It proposes borrowing open-source certification models instead of audits.
items.title: 'Human-First' Is a Promise Nobody Can Check Yet

items.excerpt: Two class actions have been filed over the breach that exposed data tied to 55.3 million Suno accounts, alleging 'negligent and/or reckless' storage. A reminder that the AI tools now sitting inside music workflows also hold creators' projects and personal data.
items.title: Two class action lawsuits filed over Suno's big data breach

items.excerpt: An Indian court found OpenAI's training on ANI's content fell under the 'private research' copyright exception, cutting the opposite way to the German GEMA v Suno ruling days earlier. For music rights holders it signals that AI training legality is fracturing by jurisdiction rather than converging.
items.title: ChatGPT training was legal and covered by 'private research' copyright exception says Indian judge
